ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in quadrilateral $ABCD$, $AD \parallel BC$, and $\angle B + \angle C = 90^\circ$. Squares $ABEF$, $ADHG$, and $DCJI$ are constructed externally on sides $AB$, $AD$, and $DC$, respectively, and their areas are denoted as $S_{1}$, $S_{2}$, and $S_{3}$ in sequence. If $S_{1} + S_{3} = 4S_{2}$, then what is the value of $\frac{BC}{AD}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, draw $AQ\parallel CD$ through point A, and let it intersect $BC$ at point Q,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle AQB=\angle QCD$,\\
$\because$ $AD\parallel BC$,\\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral $ADCQ$ is a parallelogram,\\
$\therefore$ $AD=QC$, $AQ=DC$, $\angle BCD=\angle AEB$,\\
$\because$ $\angle ABC+\angle BCD=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ABC+\angle QCD=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle BAQ=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $AB^{2}+AQ^{2}=BQ^{2}$, that is, $AB^{2}+DC^{2}=BQ^{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ $S_{1}+S_{3}=BQ^{2}$,\\
Furthermore, $\because$ $S_{1}+S_{3}=4S_{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ $4S_{2}=BQ^{2}=4AD^{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ $BQ=2AD$,\\
$\therefore$ $BC=BQ+QC=2AD+AD=3AD$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{BC}{AD}=\frac{3AD}{AD}=\boxed{3}$.

Let p be the vector from B to A and q be the vector from D to C. Because angle B is the angle between p and the positive base direction, while angle C is the angle between the negative base direction and C to D, the condition angle B + angle C = 90° implies p is perpendicular to q. Also, from the quadrilateral path B to A to D to C, vector BC = p + vector AD + q. Since BC and AD are parallel horizontal vectors, p + q is also horizontal; from the pictured convex order it points along BC and has length L - d. 推理：取 x 轴沿平行的底边方向。设 d = AD，L = BC。令 p = 向量BA，q = 向量DC。角B是 p 与正向底边方向的夹角；角C是负向底边方向与向量CD = -q 的夹角。因为角B + 角C = 90°，所以这两条斜边对应的方向互余，从而 p ⟂ q。沿路径 B→A→D→C，有 向量BC = p + 向量AD + q。由于 BC 和 AD 都是水平向右的向量，所以 p + q 也是水平向右；由图中凸形位置和 BC 比 AD 长可知 |p + q| = L - d。又因为 p ⟂ q，所以 |p + q|^2 = |p|^2 + |q|^2 = AB^2 + DC^2。正方形面积给出 S1 = AB^2，S2 = AD^2 = d^2，S3 = DC^2，因此 |p + q|^2 = S1 + S3 = 4S2 = 4d^2。于是 |p + q| = 2d，即 L - d = 2d，所以 L = 3d。因此 BC/AD = L/d = 3。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in quadrilateral $ABCD$, $AD \parallel BC$, and $\angle B + \angle C = 90^\circ$. Squares $ABEF$, $ADHG$, and $DCJI$ are constructed externally on sides $AB$, $AD$, and $DC$, respectively, and their areas are denoted as $S_{1}$, $S_{2}$, and $S_{3}$ in sequence. If $S_{1} + S_{3} = 4S_{2}$, then what is the value of $\frac{BC}{AD}$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, draw $AQ\parallel CD$ through point A, and let it intersect $BC$ at point Q,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle AQB=\angle QCD$,\\
$\because$ $AD\parallel BC$,\\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral $ADCQ$ is a parallelogram,\\
$\therefore$ $AD=QC$, $AQ=DC$, $\angle BCD=\angle AEB$,\\
$\because$ $\angle ABC+\angle BCD=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ABC+\angle QCD=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle BAQ=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $AB^{2}+AQ^{2}=BQ^{2}$, that is, $AB^{2}+DC^{2}=BQ^{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ $S_{1}+S_{3}=BQ^{2}$,\\
Furthermore, $\because$ $S_{1}+S_{3}=4S_{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ $4S_{2}=BQ^{2}=4AD^{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ $BQ=2AD$,\\
$\therefore$ $BC=BQ+QC=2AD+AD=3AD$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{BC}{AD}=\frac{3AD}{AD}=\boxed{3}$
raw_record.final_cot: First describe the figure: in the figure, the upper side AD of quadrilateral ABCD is parallel to the lower side BC, B and C are below, A and D are above; on the outside of the three sides AB, AD, and DC, squares ABEF, ADHG, and DCJI are constructed respectively, and their areas are labeled in order as S1, S2, and S3. Reasoning: draw the auxiliary line as specified, through A draw AQ ∥ CD, intersecting BC at Q. Because AD ∥ BC, and AQ ∥ CD, quadrilateral ADCQ is a parallelogram, giving QC = AD and AQ = DC. Also because Q is on BC, ∠ABQ = ∠B; and AQ ∥ CD, so ∠AQB = ∠C. It is known that ∠B + ∠C = 90°, therefore in triangle ABQ, ∠ABQ + ∠AQB = 90°, and thus ∠BAQ = 90°. Then by the Pythagorean theorem, AB^2 + AQ^2 = BQ^2. Since AQ = DC, AB^2 + DC^2 = BQ^2. The square areas satisfy S1 = AB^2, S2 = AD^2, and S3 = DC^2, therefore S1 + S3 = BQ^2. It is also known that S1 + S3 = 4S2, so BQ^2 = 4AD^2, hence BQ = 2AD. Finally, from the figure, Q is on BC and QC = AD, obtaining BC = BQ + QC = 2AD + AD = 3AD, so BC/AD = 3.
